attacks.claim: The public Recent signers panel renders each signer's full name and postal code, violating the agreed rule that public signer lists show at most first name, last initial and city. Once live and CDN-cached, the exposure is public and persistent.

The organizer-updates consent checkbox is pre-ticked. GDPR Art. 7 and PECR require a clear affirmative act for marketing-style contact, so consent collected this way is not valid for EU signers. The wording also bundles unnamed 'others' campaigns and is vague about purpose and recipient.
attacks.evidence: <input type="checkbox" id="news" name="newsletter_opt_in" value="1" checked>; Keep me updated about this campaign and others from {{ petition.organizer.name }}

attacks.claim: Signing a petition reveals political opinion, which is special-category data under GDPR Art. 9. The artifact names no Art. 9(2) condition and no DPIA for a launch that publishes signer identities.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: any Art. 9 basis or DPIA for political-opinion data; sign form is for "any open petition" with full name, email and postal code

attacks.claim: The sign form has no privacy notice, controller identity, purposes, or retention statement at the point of collection (GDPR Art. 13). No retention period for confirmed signatures and no erasure path is given; the only retention rule covers unconfirmed signatures.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: privacy notice or link on sign form; the only retention rule is "purged after 7 days", which covers unconfirmed signatures only

attacks.claim: Data-subject rights are not described: no erasure, access or consent-withdrawal path for signers. The rollback flips a flag and leaves stored signatures in place.
attacks.evidence: Rollback: flip `petitions_signing` off; sign form is replaced by the existing "Follow this petition" button.

attacks.claim: EU residency depends on postal-code resolution, with unresolvable codes stored in us-east-1. EU residents can therefore be stored outside the EU with no stated transfer mechanism, and the handling of unresolvable EU signers is unspecified. Region routing on postal code alone is also unreliable because codes overlap across countries.
attacks.evidence: stored in `signatures` (Postgres, eu-central-1 for EU-resolved postal codes, us-east-1 otherwise)

attacks.claim: The duplicate-signature 409 confirms whether a given email has already signed a specific petition, letting anyone probe political-opinion data by email address. It needs a non-disclosing response or rate limiting.

Field errors are conveyed only by red border and background colour. No error text is written into the live region, and inputs have no aria-invalid or aria-describedby link, so screen reader users get no error text and colour is the only cue (WCAG 1.4.1, 3.3.1).
attacks.evidence:
form.elements[name].classList.add('is-invalid');

(JS never sets its text); ABSENT: aria-invalid or aria-describedby on inputs

attacks.claim: Failure responses other than 422 and 2xx produce no feedback. A 409 duplicate, a 5xx, or a network exception (no catch around fetch) leaves the user on the form with no message, announcement or focus change, which is a silent failure for keyboard and screen reader users.
attacks.evidence: if (res.status === 422) {...} if (res.ok) window.location = res.headers.get('Location'); (no else branch, no catch); QA: "Duplicate signature (same email) rejected with 409"

attacks.claim: The WCAG 2.1 AA commitment is not verified. The only accessibility evidence is an automated axe-core scan of the sign page, with no manual keyboard or screen reader testing, and the Recent signers panel, error states and live count are not covered.
attacks.evidence: | axe-core automated scan on sign page | 0 violations |; ABSENT: keyboard-only or screen reader test results for sign flow, error states, or petition page counts

attacks.claim: Live signature counts refresh every 15 seconds with no live-region semantics, so assistive technology users are not told the count changed. A naive live region would announce every poll, so this needs an explicit decision.
attacks.evidence: Signature counts update live (polling every 15s, cached at the CDN for 10s).; ABSENT: aria-live or status role on the count element

attacks.claim: If a 422 response returns an empty `fields` array, `fields[0]` is undefined and `.focus()` throws. Behaviour for unknown field names is also unspecified.
attacks.evidence: const { fields } = await res.json(); for (const name of fields) form.elements[name].classList.add('is-invalid'); form.elements[fields[0]].focus();

attacks.claim: The 'Recent signers' claim of the 20 most recent confirmed signers has no ordering specified in the template or release notes, so the QA claim cannot be verified against the code.

Rollout gates only on error and bounce rates, with no monitoring of signer data exposure. The 10% rollout is by petition page rather than user, so the consent and display defects would reach all visitors on the selected pages.
attacks.evidence: Watch `sign_submit_error_rate` (< 0.5%) and confirmation email bounce rate (< 2%) for 24h.

attacks.claim: The rollback plan does not address signatures already collected or the public Recent signers exposure during rollback.
attacks.evidence: Rollback: flip `petitions_signing` off; sign form is replaced by the existing "Follow this petition" button.

attacks.claim: The QA report has no privacy-specific check on the public panel's displayed fields, and the axe scan covers only the sign page, not the Recent signers panel or error states. The panel defect would not be caught by the listed tests.
attacks.evidence: | axe-core automated scan on sign page | 0 violations |

attacks.claim: EU signer email addresses go to Postmark, a US processor, but the artifact cites only a DPA and no transfer mechanism (SCCs or EU-US Data Privacy Framework) for the EU-to-US transfer.
attacks.evidence: Confirmation emails go through Postmark; DPA countersigned 2026-09-14, listed in the public subprocessor page.

attacks.claim: Full name and postal code are collected for every signature with no stated justification, and postal code is used to select storage region.
attacks.evidence: Residents can sign any open petition with full name, email and postal code.

attacks.claim: Organizer CSV exports put signer contact data in the hands of organizers, who are separate controllers. Roles, lawful basis for the transfer, and exported fields are not stated.
attacks.evidence: Organizers can export signers who opted in to updates as CSV; export is rate-limited and audit-logged.
